claims.text: Titanium alloys can exhibit temperature-dependent plastic deformation.
The temperature-dependent plastic deformation of titanium alloys is caused by their microstructural properties.
Dislocation mobility mediates the response of the titanium alloy to temperature variation.
Grain-boundary sliding mediates the response of the titanium alloy to temperature variation.
Thermally activated dislocation glide contributes to plastic deformation in the titanium alloy.
Grain-boundary diffusion contributes to plastic deformation in the titanium alloy.
Plastic deformation increases as temperature increases from 20°C toward 500°C under uniaxial tensile loading.
The magnitude and temperature dependence of the response vary with alloy composition.
The magnitude and temperature dependence of the response vary with processing history.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome is increased plastic deformation, but the falsification rule requires both yield strength and strain at failure to increase. Increased plastic deformation does not necessarily imply increased yield strength, so the rule does not directly correspond to the stated prediction.
